title: Making a product from its recipe
summary: Turn an item's recipe into a work order, take its components out of stock and receive the finished product.

steps.text: Open the item and choose its {tab} tab. The recipe there lists the components and the quantity of each that one unit takes, so a recipe for pressed rapeseed oil lists the seed.
Say what to make and how many: add the item and quantity to a production order from {so} and finalize it. The line then shows on {dp}.
On {dp}, tick the line and choose Make selected from the Action list. This creates the work order for that item and quantity.
Open {wip}, tick the work order and choose {issue}. The components leave stock and are held as work in progress, and a work order that was still planned starts.
When the product is made, tick the work order and choose {complete}. The finished item is received into stock and the components held for it are used up.

A work order can make more than one product. If pressing rapeseed also gives oil cake, add the cake to the oil's recipe under {also}, with the quantity one batch yields and its share of the cost. Each work order then receives the cake into stock beside the oil, and the cost of the run is split between them by those shares.
You can also ask the assistant to create the work order, issue its components or complete it. It shows each change as a card and makes it only when you confirm.
